reason: Aaron, who holds elite status as the high priest and brother of Moses, is portrayed distinctly unfavorably in this passage. He capitulates to the people's demand for idolatrous worship, fashions the golden calf, constructs an altar, and when confronted by Moses, attempts to shift blame to the people rather than accepting responsibility. His response ('I asked for gold, and they gave it to me, and out came this calf') represents a dereliction of religious and moral leadership. The text emphasizes his weakness and complicity in leading the Israelites into apostasy, suggesting that even the leadership—who should maintain spiritual standards—succumbed to idolatrous impulses.
